dw.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
dw.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

dw.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
dw.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

dw.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
dw.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. Standardized to 'افت هد' suite-wide for fa and fixed dw_/hw_ labels in lib/lang.ec.fa.php to match. dw.context: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor. Dimensionless coefficient in the Darcy-Weisbach head loss equation. Distinct from Hazen-Williams C coefficient.
dw.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term. In some languages, 'friction' and 'resistance' terms compete — prefer 'friction' to match the Darcy-Weisbach naming convention. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 km re-translation): km was 'កត្តាស្ទះ' (literally 'blockage/obstruction factor', wrong sense — ស្ទះ means 'clogged/blocked', not 'friction'), contradicting the file's own established usage: dw_friction_factor and mhp_f both already use 'កត្តាកកិត' (កកិត = friction/rubbing) in lib/lang.ec.km.php. Corrected to 'កត្តាកកិត' to match established incumbent usage. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): glossary ps value was 'د مالښ ضریب' (مالښ, a native Pashto word for friction/rubbing), but مالښ does not occur anywhere in lib/lang.ec.ps.php — the file's own established word for 'friction' is اصطکاک (14+ occurrences: dw_friction_factor, mpf_friction_slope, mphl_friction_slope, mphl_friction_loss, etc.), already correctly used in dw_friction_factor's existing string 'د اصطکاک فاکتور، f'. Kept dw_friction_factor unchanged and standardized the glossary to 'د اصطکاک فاکتور' to match established incumbent usage, same defect class as the km fix above. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am bare-transliteration 'ፍሪክሽን ፋክተር' corrected to real word 'ግጭት ፋክተር' (matches shipped dw_friction_factor/dw_friction_factor_method).

dw.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
dw.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

dw.context: Flow regime in which fluid moves in parallel layers with no lateral mixing. Reynolds number below ~2000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Nearly always a direct cognate or borrowing from the Latin in technical languages. Confirm the local engineering convention.

dw.context: Flow regime between laminar and turbulent — Reynolds number roughly 2000–4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Use the adjective form meaning 'between two states'. Some languages use 'critical flow' for this regime — check local hydraulics convention.

dw.context: Flow regime with chaotic, irregular mixing. Reynolds number above ~4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
dw.translation_notes: Nearly always a cognate. Some languages distinguish 'turbulent' (adjective) from 'turbulence' (noun) — use the adjective form.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers. zh CORRECTED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 QA): the wave-2 zh translating agent initially deviated to the generic academic term '灌水器' throughout ip_ keys, reasoning that the calculator's emitter-exponent model (x from ~0 to 0.5) is generic rather than drip-only. Reverted to the established glossary field term '滴头' (dripper) for suite-wide consistency with the ar/es/uk pattern above — this glossary's own policy is field-term-over-academic-generality across all languages, and a generic hydraulic model doesn't change what practitioners actually call the part.

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file). Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): tr confirmed on dağılım düzgünlüğü — transliteration+wrong-word forms Uniformluk/Dağıtım were corrected across 7 keys.

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות. Wave-1 coinages (2026-07, category-4 sprint): fr="uniformité de distribution du quart inférieur", ro="Uniformitatea Distribuției de sfert inferior", ru="равномерность распределения по нижней четверти", uk="рівномірність розподілу по низькій чверті", bg="равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт", sr="равномерност расподеле нижег квартила", hr="jednolikost distribucije niske grupe", cs="Uniformita distribuce nízké čtvrtiny", tr="düşük-çeyrek Dağıtım Uniformluğu", id="Keseragaman Distribusi kuartal-bawah". es/pt/it/de already had glossary coverage pre-sprint. Not yet native-reviewed. ur ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 sprint): "نچلی چوتھائی تقسیم یکسانیت" (lower-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the established ur terms چوتھائی (quarter), تقسیم (distribution), یکسانیت (uniformity, already glossary term for plain "distribution uniformity"). Not yet native-reviewed. hi ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'निम्न-चतुर्थांश वितरण एकरूपता' (low-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the glossary's own hi="वितरण एकरूपता" for the base "distribution uniformity" term and prefixes "निम्न-चतुर्थांश" (low-quarter), matching the wave-1 pattern of naming the concept literally (fr/ru/uk/id etc.) rather than inventing a new metaphor. NOTE: the hi ip_ file's own pre-sprint text mistakenly used 'पाठ्यपुस्तक' (textbook) where the current English source says 'standard' — corrected to 'मानक' (standard) in lib/lang.ec.hi.php during this sprint; do not reintroduce पाठ्यपुस्तक. ar ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'انتظام التوزيع للربع الأدنى' (uniformity of distribution of the lowest quarter) reuses the glossary's own ar="انتظام التوزيع" base term for plain "distribution uniformity" (switched suite-wide in this sprint from a prior 'توحيد' root to 'انتظام', which better conveys 'evenness' rather than 'unification') and appends 'للربع الأدنى' (of the lowest quarter), naming the concept literally like the fr/ru/uk/id wave-1 coinages. Where the English source's own qualifier 'standard' appears in context (ip_du_estimate, ip_notes_3_def), it is rendered inline as 'القياسي' immediately after this base phrase, kept out of the pure glossary term here for parity with the other languages' entries. bn ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'নিম্ন-চতুর্থাংশ বিতরণ সমতা' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own bn="বিতরণ সমতা" base term, naming the concept literally. fa ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'یکنواختی توزیع ربع پایین' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own fa="یکنواختی توزیع" base term; where English says "standard" it is rendered inline as "استاندارد" immediately after this base phrase, same pattern as ar.

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation. Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): hi 'सिंचाई दर' (irrigation rate) drift standardized to file-dominant अनुप्रयोग term (ip_pr='अनुप्रयोग दर'); am confirmed on ልፍፍ.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong). Bisection is the numerical root-finding method used to close the pressure loop in the Irrigation Pressure notes. (Wave 0, 2026-07-07, removed the former "right at the takeoff" and "draw off" wording from the English source.) Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): confirmed the single suite term per language — ar=قطاع (harmonized from a مقطع/قطاع split, مقطع left meaning cross-section) and ur=حصہ (harmonized from پہنچ in cs_ vs transliterated ریچ in ip_).

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška"). Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): confirmed he=עומד מהירות (literal ראש 'head' calque removed) and sw=kimo cha kasi (Kichwa cha kasi calque removed).

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Symbol h_f (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per label-normalization decision item 90, 2026-07-07). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure table column.
ip.translation_notes: Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 'ፍሪክሽን ኪሳራ' transliteration corrected to 'ግጭት ኪሳራ' (matches shipped mphl_friction_loss); same 'friction' fix applied across 5 keys.

ip.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

ip.context: The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. NEVER calque word-by-word: es "Linea de Grado de Energia", fr "ligne d'energie grade", it "Linea di Grado Energia", ro "Linia Gradului Energetic", bg/uk "line of the energy class", cs "energy layer" are all wrong renderings found in shipped files. Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): uk must be лінія енергії — the wrong-concept calque 'лінія питомої енергії' (specific-energy line, a distinct concept) was removed; cs 'energy layer' also corrected to grade line.
Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

ip.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

mi.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
mi.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

mi.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
mi.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

mi.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mi.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): previous sw value 'radius ya maji' (literally 'radius of water', English loanword 'radius' + 'of water') named the substance rather than the hydraulic-geometry property, and did not read as an engineering term. Changed to 'radiasi ya kihaidroliki' (radius + 'hydraulic', adjectival ki- form), matching the '[radius] + hydraulic' construction used by fr/de/it/es/ro/tr (rayon hydraulique / hydraulischer Radius / raggio idraulico / radio hidráulico / raza hidraulică / hidrolik yarıçap). Used in lib/lang.ec.sw.php's mpf_hydraulic_radius.

mi.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mi.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use. Task 109 stages 4 & 5 (2026-07-19): bg wrong-word 'навлажнен' (moistened) corrected to 'омокрен' in mpf_wetted_perimeter (stage 4) and cs_notes_3_def (stage 5); km គ្រែទឹក (water bed) also confirmed corrected to glossary បរិវេណសើម (stage 4).

mi.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mi.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'. TYPO FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ru/uk transliterations were single-н 'Манинга'/'Манінга', flagged by the ru wave-1 agent as inconsistent with the established double-н transliteration ('Маннинга'/'Маннінга') used 11+ times elsewhere in both lang files (predates this sprint). Corrected to double-н for consistency. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 3-way 'roughness' spelling drift standardized to file-dominant ሻካሪነት (was ሻካርነት); it confirmed on scabrezza and sw on usuguo (both already glossary-correct).

mi.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
mi.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

mi.context: A channel whose cross-section is non-uniform / non-prismatic — a natural or surveyed section defined by station-elevation points, as opposed to a regular trapezoidal shape. Titles the Manning Irregular Channel calculator (mi_) and, in the geometric sense, the Weir Flow Irregular calculator (wi_).
mi.translation_notes: "Irregular" here is GEOMETRIC: the cross-section is non-uniform / natural / arbitrary shape. It is NOT the temporal sense "sporadic / occasional / not-regular" (bg "нередовен" WRONG, uk "нерегулярний" WRONG per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md), and NOT "incorrect / faulty" (ru "неправильное русло" reads as "wrong channel" — prefer "произвольного сечения"). Where the language allows, name the cross-section explicitly ("of irregular cross-section") rather than a bare adjective that could be read as temporal or evaluative. Task 98 audit (2026-07-13): uk/ru were already fixed to the geometric sense, but bg was still shipping the evaluative-sense defect this note itself warns against — "неправилно сечение" (= "incorrect/wrong cross-section"), across 7 occurrences (mi_menu, mi_main_title, mi_main_desc, wi_menu, wi_main_title, wi_main_desc, irr_card_canal_desc). Fixed to "произволно сечение" ("arbitrary cross-section"), a direct grammatical parallel to the Russian fix. Lesson: a documented glossary warning doesn't guarantee every flagged language was actually corrected — verify current shipped state, don't assume a note describes present reality.

odt.context: A submerged or free-flowing opening through which water discharges under head. Appears in Orifice Flow and Orifice Drain Time calculators.
odt.translation_notes: In irrigation contexts, often the opening of a headgate or pipe turnout. Use the hydraulic engineering term, not a general word for 'hole' or 'opening'. Task 109 stage 3 (2026-07-19): zh confirmed on 孔口 — the tooltip 'opening' drift 开口 in or_width was aligned.

odt.context: Coefficient correcting theoretical orifice or weir flow for real-world contraction and friction effects. Appears in Orifice and Weir calculators.
odt.translation_notes: The 'discharge' here refers to flow rate, not the verb. Use the hydraulic engineering compound term. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): ur confirmed on عامل (the suite coefficient/factor unification); ar mphl_total_junction_k_short aligned to the فاقِد loss-root used across the mphl_ cluster.

odt.context: Water surface elevation on the upstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Weir Flow and Orifice calculators.
odt.translation_notes: 'Headwater' is an upstream water surface — do not confuse with 'head' (energy) or 'source' (origin of a stream). Use the hydraulic structure term. CORRECTED 2026-07 (category-2 sprint): tr was swapped with tailwater elevation ('mansap' is Turkish for downstream, not upstream — 'memba' is upstream); fixed to 'memba su seviyesi', matching the suite's existing correct usage in lib/lang.ec.tr.php. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): confirmed bn=উজান (transliteration হেডওয়াটার removed), de=Oberwasserstand (Einstauhöhe/Einstaupegel drift removed), fa=آب بالادست (هد آب calque removed), my=ရေတက်ဘက်ရေ (ဦးရေ/ခေါင်းရေ ambiguous-term removed); sw must avoid the 'kichwa' anatomical-head calque.

odt.context: Water surface elevation on the downstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Orifice Flow calculator. When tailwater is above the invert, the orifice is submerged.
odt.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic structure term for downstream water level. Pair consistently with 'headwater elevation'. CORRECTED 2026-07 (category-2 sprint): tr was swapped with headwater elevation; fixed to 'mansap su seviyesi' (downstream), matching the suite's existing correct usage in lib/lang.ec.tr.php. Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): confirmed bn=ভাটি (টেলওয়াটার transliteration removed) and de=Unterwasserstand.

odt.context: The top (highest point) of the inside of a pipe or of an opening. Synonyms: top, soffit, obvert. Technical hydraulics term; orifice flow applies only when headwater is above the crown of the opening.
odt.translation_notes: Prefer the local hydraulics term for the pipe soffit/crown if one exists; otherwise a plain word for 'top (of the opening)' is correct. Not the royal or anatomical senses of 'crown'.

previous_translated.english: Darcy-Weisbach Pipe Head Loss at Given Diameter, Roughness, and Flow

next_translated.value: Apsolutna visina hrapavosti, e, stijenke cijevi. Tipične vrijednosti: čelik (novi) 0,046 mm, čelik (rabljeni) 0,15 mm, HDPE 0,003 mm, PVC/uPVC 0,0015 mm, beton 0,3–3 mm.
next_translated.english: Absolute roughness height, e, of the pipe wall. Typical values: steel (new) 0.046 mm, steel (used) 0.15 mm, HDPE 0.003 mm, PVC/uPVC 0.0015 mm, concrete 0.3–3 mm.

next_translated.value: t = √H<sub>1</sub> / (C<sub>d</sub> A<sub>or</sub> √(2g)) × (2A<sub>x</sub>/5 + 8√(A<sub>x</sub>A<sub>0</sub>)/15 + 16A<sub>0</sub>/15) daje vrijeme pražnjenja od visine H do otvora. Vrijeme pražnjenja = t(H<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>) − t(H<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>), gdje je H<sub>1</sub> = početna kota − kota otvora, H<sub>2</sub> = završna kota − kota otvora.
next_translated.english: t = √H<sub>1</sub> / (C<sub>d</sub> A<sub>or</sub> √(2g)) × (2A<sub>x</sub>/5 + 8√(A<sub>x</sub>A<sub>0</sub>)/15 + 16A<sub>0</sub>/15) gives drain time from head H to the orifice. Drain time = t(H<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>) − t(H<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>), where H<sub>1</sub> = starting elevation − orifice elevation, H<sub>2</sub> = ending elevation − orifice elevation.
